clesRetenues: Q Sebastian G. (shareholder, Say Technologies) - progress on the dividend tracker: launch planned this year, the team having identified an opportunity to pay dividends 17 to 23 days earlier than competitors by exploiting the timing of the record date.

Q Matt S. (shareholder, Say Technologies) - will Robinhood have access to the next large IPOs: management declines to name specific deals but confirms a radical change since 2021 (retail allocations discouraged) towards allocations of 20-30% now requested by founders themselves.

Q Alexander Markgraff (KeyBanc) - customer growth strategy beyond Trump Accounts: simplified onboarding, marketing targeted at high-ROI activities, organisation of the product catalogue to avoid cluttering the interface.

Q Markgraff (follow-up) - flexibility of the OpEx framework for the rest of the year: 85-90% of costs are fixed, discretionary spending is reassessed on an ongoing basis, with marketing and variable costs offering levers for adjustment if needed.

Q Dan Fannon (Jefferies) - resilience of the customer base in a period of volatility, April trends by asset class: net deposits of 18 Md$ in Q1 despite macro headwinds, diversification via banking/card/robo-advisor (Strategies); April shows the best equities/options volumes of the year, prediction markets ~3 Md$ (2nd best month).

Q Jeff Roberts (journalist) - is the prediction markets market heading towards a duopoly or several players: consolidation expected from dozens of exchanges towards a few leaders, Robinhood advantages cited (27M funded accounts, Rothera partnership with Susquehanna).

Q Devin Ryan (Citizens) - impact of the removal of the PDT rule, link with agentic trading: removal judged positive, an outdated notion linking account balance and sophistication, friction removed for retail participation, fitting into the broader agentic AI strategy.

Q Dan Dolev (Mizuho) - details on agentic trading: refusal to disclose specifics ahead of launch, announcements expected at the May product launch, at the July crypto event and at the autumn HOOD Summit.

Q Steven Chubak (Wolfe) - securities lending outlook, IPO tailwinds, take rate dynamics in Q2: 25% customer opt-in, 50% of assets in the fully-paid programme, room for progress; take rate treated as an output metric, focus on market share; April shows a rebound vs the Q1 troughs.

Q Benjamin Budish (Barclays) - margin funding strategy, movement of the bank cash sweep: 6 Md$ of cash sweep moved onto the balance sheet to fund margin with no customer impact, ~25% of free credit balances should remain in sweep, ~6 Md$ on the balance sheet, standard brokerage practice.

Q Craig Siegenthaler (BofA) - timetable for AI-driven financial advisers: two distinct meanings distinguished (regulatorily compliant trading recommendations vs full financial advice including banking/estate/tax); Robinhood Strategies (fiduciary robo-advisor), TradePMR for human advisers, self-serve solutions in pilot (concierge/estate planning).

Q James Yaro (Goldman Sachs) - crypto stabilisation outlook, volume trends, long-term take rates: focus on the real utility of tokenisation rather than on predicting the Bitcoin price, less than 20% of revenue coming from crypto, highly diversified; resilient institutional growth, Bitstamp gaining share.

Q Patrick Moley (Piper Sandler) - progress update on perpetual futures, US expansion timetable: EU perpetuals performing well on Bitstamp, customers asking for more leverage; the US launch requires regulatory changes, the industry's current offering being long-dated futures rather than true perpetuals; discussions under way with regulators, ready to launch upon approval.

Q Tannor Manson (Future Investing) - impact of the AI hiring strategy, efficiency gains across the organisation: 100 M$ of efficiency in Q2025 mainly from customer service and engineering, volumes up 50% with headcount stable, no staff reduction but growth absorbed through AI productivity, adoption above 90% of employees.

Q Brian Bedell (Deutsche Bank) - mix of active/less active traders, composition of customer deposits, interactions with crypto: Gold attach rate up to 40% for new customers (against a low single digit previously), high-yield cash and interest on options collateral as adoption drivers; crypto constituency distinct but integrated into the platform.

Q David Smith (Truist) - banking growth drivers (new customers vs ARPU expansion): expansion currently driven by Gold among existing customers, with the opportunity shifting towards new customer acquisition via the Gold Card as the main lead product.

Q John Todaro (Needham) - Bitstamp institutional expansion, details on institutional lending: institutional customers asking for operational improvements (batch processing, throughput), institutional lending centred on working capital/overnight liquidity needs, a product with no credit risk using the company's balance sheet.

Q Amit Kukreja (Amit is Investing) - international expansion strategy, market entry approach: crypto and brokerage offerings on a global scale, full licensing in selected markets (Singapore, Indonesia, United Kingdom), with tokenisation accelerating coverage of long-tail markets.

Q Ramsey El-Assal (Cantor Fitzgerald) - level of engagement in Trump Accounts, cross-sell plans: a long-term opportunity with the next generation, priority given to the best government product ever built rather than to near-term cross-monetisation.

Q Edward Engel (Compass Point) - April crypto volume trends relative to Q1: no notable change, marked rebound in equities/options, prediction markets ~3 Md$ (2nd best month), margin continuing to grow, crypto in the same zone as in Q1.

Q Michael Cyprys (Morgan Stanley) - API connectivity strategy, use cases, multi-year opportunity: historical focus on proprietary experiences, now interest in API offerings given the agentic AI direction, low-cost provider with solid infrastructure.

Q Dr. Roy (Crossroads Capital) - public sector expansion, multiple government opportunities: new territory for Robinhood, learning about government contracts, other states and international enquiries expressing interest, focus on the current success of Trump Accounts before expanding.

Q Craig Maurer (FT Partners) - state-level concerns on prediction markets, impact on the momentum: a rational jurisdictional dispute, with the CFTC claiming federal jurisdiction, Robinhood backing the CFTC position, an issue that will play out over several years.

Q Journalist (Stock Market News) - expansion plans for Robinhood Social: launched with HOOD Summit attendees, extended to 10 000 customers, weekly feature releases, general availability expected in the coming months.

Q Zach (shareholder, Say Technologies) - mass-market launch timetable for Robinhood Social: target of rolling out by the end of Q3, iteration under way on feed algorithms and features ahead of general availability.

Q John (shareholder, Say Technologies) - which aspects of the Clarity Act would have the most impact for Robinhood: tokenisation benefits and regulatory stability highlighted, Robinhood will innovate in any case but the Clarity Act would allow the product potential to be maximised.

Q Joe (shareholder, Say Technologies) - traction of Trump Accounts since the July launch (sign-ups, asset flows): 7 million children enrolled with 1,5 Md$ of contributions, tens of millions of accounts expected with rapid growth continuing.

Q Dan Dolev (Mizuho) - structural components of the growth of nearly 1 million funded accounts: attributed to a supportive macro backdrop, new products (banking, credit card), the SpaceX IPO, contributions from acquisitions and overseas expansion.

Q Daniel Fannon - durability of prediction markets beyond World Cup momentum: a sustained events calendar (football, midterm elections), continuous product improvements, and the ramp-up of Rothera as drivers of durability.

Q David Smith (Truist) - split of prediction markets users between new customers and adoption by the existing base: customers adopt several products whatever the entry point, with prediction markets users now approaching 2 million in total.

Q Devin Ryan (Citizens) - first customer learnings on agentic trading and roadmap for version 2.0: more than 100 000 active accounts, rising volumes, plans to broaden the toolkit while simplifying the user interface.

Q Christian Blue (Autonomous) - vision for expanding Rothera beyond its status as 3rd DCM: plans for continued growth and potential expansion into perpetuals, multi-venue routing to ensure best execution for customers.

Q Ramsey El-Assal (Cantor) - next growth opportunities in DeFi beyond current tokenised assets and lending: developer momentum, partnerships leveraging real-world assets (RWA), infrastructure improvements, broadening of asset class tokenisation.

Q James Yarrow (Goldman Sachs) - timetable and regulatory obstacles for the US perpetual futures launch: constructive discussions with the CFTC progressing, with no precise timetable but a confirmed commitment to offer perpetuals.

Q Daniel (Crossroads) - plans to add support for foreign equities: confirmed on the agenda for global expansion, infrastructure complexity acknowledged but priority given to developing an international marketplace.

Q John (Artemis) - long-term upside potential of Robinhood Chain enabling global access to the app: real-world assets as a unique contribution, developer momentum, permissionless nature enabling diverse use cases.

Q Ahmed - durability of the engagement flywheel to support the trillion-dollar vision: product quality, cross-sell flywheel via Gold subscriptions, customer experience orchestrated across the whole product range.

Q Alexander (ButtonAdvisor) - path to a trillion-dollar valuation, what makes the target more reachable than before, role of AI: agentic finance, global access to assets via blockchain, private markets, multiple growth vectors cited.

Q Craig Maurer (FT Partners) - comment on the decline in July net deposits vs Q2, customer health: full-year growth still above the 20% target, the variance attributed to seasonality and macro factors, customer engagement confirmed as solid.

Q Steven Chubak (Wolfe) - breakdown of the expense guidance: self-funding of the new initiatives (Rothera/WonderFi) while maintaining the efficiency of the legacy base, allowing a guidance cut despite the product expansion.

Q Craig Siegenthaler (BofA) - product rollout strategy in Asia following the Singapore MAS licence: launching several products simultaneously rather than sequentially, Singapore as the hub for South-East Asia.

Q Alexander Markgraff (KeyBanc) - how DeFi changes customer engagement and monetisation vs traditional products: engagement driven by developers via Twitter/podcasts, a few basis points per transaction with ~50% revenue sharing with Arbitrum.

Q Brian Bedell (Deutsche Bank) - interest in launching Cboe-style financial KPI contracts, timetable for migrating NFL event contracts to Rothera: uncertainty on the securities regime, multi-counterparty strategy highlighted, majority of the flow expected via Rothera over the medium term.

Q Patrick Moley (Piper Sandler) - why not a more aggressive launch of US perpetuals given competitor moves and earlier support: hesitancy denied, a full product roadmap and multiple growth vectors cited, commitment confirmed with no precise timetable.
Q Benjamin Budish (Barclays) - July ADV metrics by product and take rate trends: equities/options/prediction markets similar to Q2; crypto slightly slower; July take rate in line with the Q2 average.

Q Edward Engel (Compass Point) - strategy of partnering with other prediction markets exchanges vs concentrating on Rothera: both approaches confirmed, diversification maintained across ForecastEx, Kalshi and Rothera while pushing Rothera flow as the priority.

Q Andrew Hardy (BTIG) - focus areas of the top-of-funnel acquisition strategy and benefit from the removal of the PDT rule: improved onboarding, product sharing, bank-brokerage cross-sell; PDT benefit judged disproportionate for Robinhood's retail base.

Q Gav (Wolfe Research) - key milestones for agentic trading and extension to prediction markets: goal of giving agents all the tools of the Robinhood trader, team momentum highlighted, announcements expected at the next active trader event.

hypothese.summary: Q2 2026 confirms the creation thesis but with a magnitude that goes far beyond the nowcast: record revenue 1,308 Md$ (+32%, creation nowcast ~1,213 Md$ - exceeded by ~8%), EPS 0,62$ (+48%, consensus beaten by 47,6%). Above all, Rothera/prediction markets is running well beyond the creation model: 156 M$ of revenue in Q2 2026 alone, against 150 M$ modelled for the FULL YEAR 2026 at creation - the central catalyst of the thesis has already been delivered at more than 100% of the annual target after a single full quarter, even before the NFL season and the November 2026 midterm elections (a major event still to come). Negative market reaction despite the beat (-3,33% on the day of the release): the market appears to judge that the good news was already largely in the price.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Robinhood is building the financial super-app: brokerage (equities/options/crypto/prediction markets), banking (Gold Card), wealth and private-markets access. Q2 2026 validated all three setup drivers (revenue diversification, near-free growth options via Rothera/Trump Accounts, capital discipline) while revealing the setup UNDERESTIMATED the prediction-markets inflection: Q2 alone generated 156M (World-Cup-boosted) versus 150M modeled for the entire year. OpEx guidance was tightened and LOWERED despite absorbing unbudgeted Rothera/WonderFi costs.

== THESIS READ ==
- Prediction markets re-rated upward in the model but Q2 was event-driven (World Cup); H2 leans on NFL season (Q3) and midterm elections (Q4) - still event-dependent revenue. Watch: a no-event quarter's run-rate.
- Cost discipline is the quiet strength: raising investment while lowering the OpEx envelope. Watch: FY27 OpEx guidance.
- The 47.6% Q2 GAAP beat is misleading (129M deconsolidation gain) - documented, not extrapolated. Watch: clean-print EPS next quarter.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Base convention: 'ebit' IS pretax income (fintech convention, net interest revenue inside the top line) - so the bridge's finNet is zero BY CONSTRUCTION and the only wedge is tax. FY24 net ABOVE pretax (1.4bn DTA release) and FY25 ETR 12.8% vs 15% normative are documented one-offs. Massive net cash (-4.3bn growing to -11.8bn).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
FY26 bottom-up by segment: S1 actual 2,378M + S2 ~2,900M (NFL Q3, midterms Q4) = ~5,278M (+18%); EBIT margin 47% (leverage demonstrated at Q2: 57% adjusted EBITDA margin). Tax 15% normative, drifting watch to 19% as DTA benefits fade - THE main below-line risk. Shares ~flat net of SBC buyback. Watch: crypto-cycle dependence; regulatory posture on prediction markets; tax-rate normalization pace.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Nov, NFL season print); midterm-election Q4 volumes; Rothera/Trump Accounts rollout; first no-event quarter run-rate.

ancrages.moteur: FY2026 revenue rebuilt bottom-up: actual H1 2026 (2 378 M$, +23% vs estimated H1 2025) + estimated H2 2026 at ~2 900 M$ (Q3 driven by the NFL season on prediction markets, Q4 driven by the November 2026 midterm elections and year-end seasonality) - revised significantly upwards vs creation (4 950 M$ -> 5 278 M$) mainly on the back of the prediction markets/Rothera trajectory, which has already exceeded the annual creation target (150 M$) in Q2 alone (156 M$).

Continued strong but gradually less spectacular growth: +18%/yr over 2027-2028 (2028 being a presidential election year, a prediction markets catalyst potentially comparable to 2026), then moderation to +12%/yr over 2029-2030 (years without a major electoral catalyst). A reconstruction assumption in the absence of quantified guidance beyond the next quarter.

EBIT margin retained at 47% for FY2026 (vs 45,7% at creation), revised upwards following confirmation of operating leverage above expectations (actual adjusted EBITDA margin of 57% in Q2, cost guidance tightened/cut despite the addition of Rothera and WonderFi, not budgeted initially). Gradual expansion continued towards 48-49% over the 2027-2030 horizon, with the Rothera mix effect (incremental margin close to 100% on that segment) continuing to pull the consolidated margin higher.

Sliding normative tax rate maintained (15% in 2026 -> 19% in 2030, starting close to the actual 2025 effective rate to avoid a false step) and normalised Net/EBIT conversion ratio maintained at ~85%, creation methodology unchanged in the absence of any new element calling it into question.

Share count kept broadly stable (~907-908M in 2026, a slight decline thereafter): buybacks continued (7,5M shares for 664 M$ YTD at Q2) offsetting SBC dilution, with the 2,2 Md$ convertible notes issue at a 0% coupon generating no net dilution as long as the share price stays below 300$ (well away from the current price).

Net cash position strengthened by the 2,2 Md$ capital raise in Q2 2026 (convertible notes), partly offset by continued buybacks (664 M$ YTD) - net cash trajectory revised upwards (more negative, hence more net cash) vs creation, with cash generation continuing over the projection horizon.

CORRECTION after a full reading of the Q2 2026 release (E5 d-bis): reported net income (573 M$, EPS 0,62$) includes a 129 M$ non-operating gain tied to the deconsolidation of Robinhood Ventures Fund I (RVI, a formerly consolidated subsidiary in which Robinhood no longer holds a majority following its listing), i.e. 0,14$/share. This gain is a one-off accounting item (remeasurement of the residual stake at fair value at the moment control was lost), unrelated to the operating performance of the quarter. It is NOT carried forward in the FY2026-2030 projection, which remains built from the adjusted EBITDA margin (already excluding this item) rather than from an extrapolation of reported GAAP EPS - but it must be explicitly excluded from any reading of the Q2 beat as evidence of operating leverage above expectations.

'Clean' EPS excluding this one-off, non-operating item: around 0,48$ (444 M$ / ~924M diluted shares), i.e. a real but more modest beat of around 14% vs consensus (0,42$) - still a beat, but on nothing like the scale of the +47,6% headline. dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quantitative Q3 revenue/EPS guidance (company policy). Strong qualitative July color: average daily volumes for equities, options and prediction markets in a similar area to record Q2 levels; crypto trending slightly slower early in the month; July take rates in a similar zone to the Q2 average. July net deposits tracking toward ~$4B (excluding Trump Accounts contributions) - management attributes the sequential slowdown to normal summer seasonality and reiterates the >20% annualized net-deposit growth target, already well exceeded YTD including July, with customers net buyers on drawdowns. Robinhood Social general rollout targeted by end of Q3; agentic trading extending to crypto; HOOD Summit (Houston) and the active-trader event as next product catalysts.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY2026 adjusted OpEx+SBC lowered AND tightened to $2.675-2.775B (from $2.7-2.825B), even while absorbing Rothera JV and WonderFi acquisition costs that were not in the prior outlook - savings spread across all three original buckets (M&A efficiency, core business, new-product seeds), with seed investment actually increased vs the start of the year; CFO frames the lean, self-funding operating model as a competitive advantage. No FY revenue or EPS guidance provided, per usual policy; long-term measurement framework offered instead: >20%/yr net deposits, Rule of 40 (Robinhood at 'Rule of 80+' at >$5B annual revenue scale), and a growing count of $100M+ ARR businesses (13 today).
pointsCles: Record, more diversified quarter: revenue $1,308M (+32% YoY, ~$27M above consensus) with transaction revenue $776M (+44%) - options $342M (+29%), equities $129M (+95%), event contracts/prediction markets $156M (~11x YoY, already above the ~$150M modeled at thesis creation for FULL-YEAR 2026) offsetting crypto at $100M (-38%); adjusted EBITDA $741M (+35%) at a 57% margin, adjusted OpEx+SBC $641M below the prior guidance range. Headline GAAP EPS $0.62 (+48%) flattered by the ~$129M RVI deconsolidation gain (~$0.14/share); stock fell ~3.3% on the print as the market saw through the one-off.

Prediction-markets infrastructure play accelerating: Rothera (JV with Susquehanna/SIG) became a top-3 US DCM one month after launch with the World Cup as proof of concept; ~2M customers have now used prediction markets (vs 1.5M last disclosed) and management expects the majority of event-contract flow to migrate to Rothera near/medium term while staying multi-homed (ForecastEx, Kalshi); Robinhood Chain monetizes at a few basis points per transaction with a ~50/50 revenue share with Arbitrum, >$12B DEX volume and fastest chain to 100M transactions (>150M to date), Robinhood Earn >$200M deposits at 7% APY (USDG).

Growth engines firing on multiple vectors: ~1M net new funded customers in Q2 (best quarter in ~5 years since IPO; macro, banking/credit card, SpaceX IPO, WonderFi ~200K accounts, international), record $22B net deposits (28% annualized), platform assets ~$369B at quarter-end (near $400B at call date), Gold at a record 4.8M subs (17% attach; 40-50% of new customers), Gold Card past 1M cardholders with >$17B annualized spend, banking >$3B deposits since November, Trump Accounts launched with 7M children enrolled and ~$1.5B contributions (Robinhood broker and sole initial trustee), agentic trading >100K accounts, PDT-rule removal (June) a multi-quarter tailwind skewed to Robinhood's small-balance base.

Discipline funding expansion: FY26 adjusted OpEx+SBC guidance LOWERED and tightened to $2.675-2.775B despite absorbing unbudgeted Rothera and WonderFi costs (savings across M&A, core and seed buckets, self-funded); 13 businesses now above $100M ARR (Robinhood Legend and the Credit Card added this quarter); $2.2B opportunistic June convertible raise at 0% coupon with no net dilution below a $300 share price, alongside 7.5M shares repurchased YTD for $664M; CFO frames the long-term scorecard as >20%/yr net deposits, Rule of 40 (currently 'Rule of 80+') and a 10x-in-10-years ambition (~$1T market-cap discussion).
